transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, I'm a teacher, so I know what that normal end-of-the-day tired feels like, but this isn't that. Even after a full night’s sleep, I still have to really push myself just to get through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning. It's just constant.
Aside from feeling constantly tired, have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah, I have. I mean, most days I can still smile for my students and get through the lessons okay. But underneath that, it just feels like there’s this... gray, flat feeling. It follows me home, and it makes even the things I usually enjoy, like my garden or my watercolors, seem really far away.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been a while. I'd say it's been going on for about two years... maybe two years and two months now. It started right around the time my husband stopped working outside the home. Our whole household routine changed back then, and, well, that's really when this all began.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting more than two months where your mood returned to normal and you felt like yourself again?

No, not really. I mean, there might be a good day here or there, maybe a weekend where I feel a little lighter, but it never lasts. It's definitely never been a whole two months where I felt completely back to normal. That gray feeling is pretty much always there in the background.
Have you noticed that you have become unusually sensitive to cold temperatures, even when people around you feel comfortable?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, my classroom can get a little drafty sometimes, but I don't feel unusually cold compared to the kids or the other teachers. I'd say I'm pretty normal when it comes to temperature.
Before this started two years ago, did you ever experience any other periods in your life where you felt depressed?

No, I don't think so. I mean, sure, I'd have a bad day here or there like anyone else, but nothing like this. Before two years ago, I always felt pretty normal. This is really the first time I've ever dealt with feeling this down.
How has your sleep been over these past two years?

My sleep has been pretty normal, honestly. I usually go to bed around the same time and wake up when my alarm goes off for school. I don't really have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. It's just... I still feel tired even when I get a full night's rest, but the sleep itself hasn't changed.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over this time?

No, not really. My appetite has been pretty steady. I still eat my normal meals, you know, pack the same kind of lunch for school every day. And my weight hasn't really fluctuated or anything. So, no, no changes there.
How has your self-esteem or confidence in yourself been over these past two years?

It hasn't been great, honestly. I just keep thinking I should be handling everything better than I am. Like with teaching, my lesson plans have been taking me twice as long to finish, and I actually had to say no to mentoring a newer teacher this year. When things like that happen, I just tell myself I’m letting my school down... and my family, too. I just don't have a lot of confidence in how I'm doing things right now.
